correctness.rationale: For any constant-preserving linear average on n sites, the step decomposition h=h_1*1+sum Delta_k h*H^(k) gives the exact adjacent-variation operator seminorm as the maximum variation of step responses; each lower-bound witness is a step. For uniform nonempty intervals, the explicitly counted difference kernel is nonnegative and endpoints of step image differ by 1-n/[n(n+1)/2]=(n-1)/(n+1), proving the all-n exact contraction. For uniform sampled length then uniform placement, rational sum over n(n+1)/2 reversals with weights 1/[n(n-l+1)] was independently reconstructed as an n-by-n Markov matrix for each 2<=n<=14; every step cut was tested using exact Fraction arithmetic. The maxima match 0,1/2,5/8,41/60,271/360,113/140,2813/3360,824/945,5689/6300,3254/3465,322507/332640,355991/360360,5105521/5045040; only n=14 exceeds 1, and exact witnesses include cuts k=5 and 9. The continuum step at t=1/3 has a downward excursion of log(2/sqrt(3)), hence total variation at least 1+log(4/3); bounded-expectation Riemann sums along 0,t+,2/3,1 transfer it to liminf finite sharp coefficients. Independent 2000/5000-mesh quadrature corroborated limit 1.287682072. Nothing asserts an exact all-n length-uniform norm or an exact asymptotic limit.
residual_risks: The continuum integral formula and Riemann convergence were reviewed analytically, not certified by a computer algebra system.
The exact first onset is certified only by exhaustive finite dimensions 2..14, combined with an all-n statement only for uniform intervals.

value.rationale: The change in sampling order, equal interval versus equal length, has a mathematically sharp and counterintuitive effect on the strongest path-BV contraction/amplification guarantee. The exact first dimension 14, nontrivial rational extremizer and explicit asymptotic witness make this a motivated stability boundary, not an arbitrary finite slice. The step-reduction technique yields a reusable exact optimization method.
